reasons: The cited clause (§20(h)) selects Nova Scotia/Canadian law and Nova Scotia courts, which is outside the accepted set (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so it fails both preferred and fallback on the material choice-of-law term — correctly classified as a deviation, not over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position exactly (New York law; exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County) while preserving the two-sentence structure and surrounding language, consistent with the redline guidance to replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; deletion of the trailing 'laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia' is necessary rather than gratuitous.

The failed changed-character-ratio check (0.601) is explained by the rule genuinely requiring replacement of both the governing-law and venue words in a short clause; no smaller edit would reach the playbook position.

The comment is accurate (Nova Scotia outside accepted list, correct fallback offer of Delaware/California/England and Wales with London courts), on-tone, concise, and properly prefixed; the rationale correctly notes the venue is non-exclusive so this stops short of walk-away, and confirms no arbitration clause elsewhere.
Severity medium is appropriate for the category and the non-exclusive (rather than mandatory foreign arbitration) forum.
